slides.headline: Welcome to the Trash Golf Association
slides.body: Golf for the rest of us.

slides.headline: You qualify if…
slides.body: You've ever apologized to a tree.

slides.headline: You also qualify if…
slides.body: Your best shot of the day was the one nobody saw.

slides.headline: Fewer blow-ups. More fun.
slides.body: Simple fixes, honest scorecards, and rules no pro would approve.

slides.headline: Membership is free.
slides.body: Follow, save, and send this to the worst golfer you know (with love).

posts.caption: Welcome to the TGA. No pure strikes required. Follow along for simple fixes, honest scorecards, and the official rules of bad golf. Tag a fellow member.

slides.headline: Volume 1
slides.body: Five rules every member lives by.

slides.headline: A shot in the trees is a new hole.
slides.body: Find the opening, take your medicine, move on.

slides.headline: Bogey is a good score.
slides.body: Double is a fine score. Triple is a story for the clubhouse.

slides.headline: The range is a lie.
slides.body: Nobody has ever hit it like that on hole 1.

slides.headline: Never apologize to a playing partner for a good shot.
slides.body: You earned it. Probably.

slides.headline: The best shot is the next one.
slides.body: Save this for your next round.

posts.caption: The official TGA Rulebook, Vol. 1. Which rule is your favorite? Save this for your next round.

slides.headline: 3 reasons you keep slicing
slides.body: And what to try about each one.

slides.headline: Your grip is too weak.
slides.body: Try seeing two knuckles on your lead hand at address. It helps the face close at impact.

slides.headline: Your path is out-to-in.
slides.body: Picture the ball sitting inside the target line and swing out toward the right-field side of the range.

slides.headline: You're swinging too hard.
slides.body: Smooth 80% beats a wild 100%. Tempo fixes more than technique.

slides.headline: Change one thing at a time.
slides.body: Pick one, hit 10 balls, and see what changes. Save this for the range.

posts.caption: Most slices come from the face being open to the path. Pick ONE of these to try at the range and see what happens. Which one sounds like you?

slides.headline: Bogey is a good score.
slides.body: Here's why.

slides.headline: Most 90s shooters make bogey or worse on every hole.
slides.body: That's 18 bogeys = 90. Not a bad day.

slides.headline: It's the double and triple.
slides.body: One blow-up hole costs more than three good ones save.

slides.headline: Aim for the fat part of the green.
slides.body: Two-putt for bogey is a win. Pars are a bonus.

slides.headline: Stop chasing hero shots.
slides.body: Send this to someone who tries one every round.

posts.caption: Golf got easier the day I started counting bogey as a win. Stop the blow-ups and the score takes care of itself.

slides.headline: 5 signs you're a TGA member
slides.body: Be honest.

slides.headline: You own more lost-ball sleeves than clubs.
You've said 'that felt good' about a shot that went 80 yards.
Your swing thought changes every hole.
You still enjoy it.
slides.body: That's the whole point. Welcome.

posts.caption: How many of these apply to you? Be honest. Comment your number.

slides.headline: Stop losing balls off the tee
slides.body: 3 tiny changes that work for high handicaps.

slides.headline: Tee up on your miss side.
slides.body: If you miss right, tee up on the right side and aim left. More fairway to work with.

slides.headline: Take less club.
slides.body: A fairway wood or hybrid in play beats a driver in the trees.

slides.headline: Pick a tiny target.
slides.body: A tree, a bunker edge, a cart path mark. A small target beats 'the fairway'.

slides.headline: Play the hole backward.
slides.body: Where do you want your second shot from? Start there.

posts.caption: Off the tee is my biggest leak too. These three habits save me strokes every round. Save for your next round.

slides.headline: How to reset after a triple bogey
slides.body: The 10-second rule.

slides.headline: Give yourself 10 seconds.
slides.body: Be mad. Sigh. Mutter. Then it's over.

slides.headline: Take one breath.
slides.body: Slow it down. Your tempo is the first thing to go.

slides.headline: Pick a new target.
slides.body: Forget the score. All that matters is the next tee shot.

slides.headline: You're playing a game.
slides.body: Send this to the member who needs it today.

posts.caption: Everyone blows up. The difference is how fast you reset. Try the 10-second rule next round.

slides.headline: The 3-putt is the real score killer
slides.body: A simple drill to stop them.

slides.headline: Most 3-putts are bad first putts.
slides.body: Not bad second putts. Distance control is the issue.

slides.headline: Pick a 30-foot putt.
slides.body: Roll 5 balls. The goal is to finish inside a 3-foot circle.

slides.headline: Lag it close, then tap in.
slides.body: Don't chase the hole from far away. Aim for 'close', not 'in'.

slides.headline: 10 minutes before your round.
slides.body: Save this for your next warm-up.

posts.caption: Stop treating 30-foot putts like they have to go in. Get it close. Try this drill before your next round.

slides.body: Nominations are closed. The winner has been chosen.

slides.headline: The guy who shot 94
slides.body: …and told everyone it was an 82.

slides.headline: Mulligans: 'practice shots'.
slides.body: Gimmes: 'inside the leather'. Drops: 'it was close'.

slides.headline: A free sleeve of lost balls.
slides.body: Tag your member of the month.

slides.headline: A 20-minute range routine
slides.body: For people with a day job.

slides.headline: Stretch and wedge shots.
slides.body: Half swings. Get the tempo right first.

slides.headline: The ball-flight round.
slides.body: Hit a few 7-irons, a few hybrids, a few drivers. Pick a target for each shot.

slides.headline: Putt to finish.
slides.body: End with a few 3-footers so the last thing you do is make something.

slides.headline: Quality beats quantity.
slides.body: Save this for your next range visit.

posts.caption: You don't need two hours at the range. 20 focused minutes beats a lazy bucket. Save this routine.

slides.headline: Hitting from the rough
slides.body: The simple rule.

slides.headline: Take more loft.
slides.body: The grass grabs the club. More loft helps the ball get out.

slides.headline: Grip a little firmer.
slides.body: Rough twists the face closed. Hold on.

slides.headline: Expect it to fly farther.
slides.body: Grass between face and ball cuts spin. That's called a flier.

slides.headline: Just get back to the fairway.
slides.body: Save this for your next round.

posts.caption: The rough wins when you get greedy. Take your medicine and get back in play.

slides.headline: What high handicaps get wrong about the driver
Swinging as hard as possible.
slides.body: Smooth tempo gets better contact, and contact is distance.

slides.headline: Teeing it too low.
slides.body: Half the ball should sit above the top of the clubface.

slides.headline: Ball too far back.
slides.body: Play it off your lead heel for a driver.

slides.headline: A fairway finder beats a bomb.
slides.body: Send this to a playing partner.

posts.caption: Hitting it 220 in the fairway beats hitting it 260 in the trees. Try these.

slides.headline: Volume 2
slides.body: Five more rules for members.

slides.headline: The ball is always 'just a little left'.
slides.body: Of where it actually went.

slides.headline: The best part of the round is the drive cart.
slides.body: Or the post-round beer.

slides.headline: Never give swing advice.
slides.body: Unless asked. Or unless you're 'just curious'.

slides.headline: One good shot cancels 17 bad ones.
slides.body: That's the whole business model.

slides.headline: Have fun. That's the only rule.
slides.body: Save and share.

posts.caption: The TGA Rulebook, Vol. 2. Which rule would you add?

slides.headline: Range vs. course
slides.body: Why they feel so different.

slides.headline: Perfect lie. No penalty. Same ball.
slides.body: You hit 10 in a row and feel like a pro.

slides.headline: Uneven lies. Nerves. One ball.
slides.body: Every swing matters, so you swing differently.

slides.headline: Practice like it's the course.
slides.body: Pick a target. Switch clubs. Hit one shot at a time.

slides.headline: The range is practice, not proof.
slides.body: Send this to a friend who swears they 'hit it great on the range'.

posts.caption: The range is practice, not proof. Try one-ball-at-a-time practice and see how it changes your round.
